Which row in the following table correctly shows three nuclei of the same element, and three
nuclei that have the same number of neutrons?

hints: Notice the proton number column fixes the element: L, M and N all share 89 while O, P and Q share 90.
Recall neutron number is not given directly but is $N = A - Z$, nucleon number minus proton number.
Compare $A - Z$ for R, P and N: $227-91$, $226-90$ and $225-89$.
walkthrough: Identify the rule for same element: same proton number $Z$. From the table L, M and N all have $Z = 89$, so they are isotopes of one element.
State the rule for neutron number: $N = A - Z$ where $A$ is nucleon number.
Calculate for the second group: for R, $N = 227 - 91 = 136$, for P, $N = 226 - 90 = 136$, for N, $N = 225 - 89 = 136$.
Check the other groupings: M, P, S have different $Z$ values, and O, P, Q have $N = 137, 136, 135$.
Only the pairing L M N for same $Z$ and R P N for same $N = 136$ satisfies both columns. This is option A.

A.explanation: L, M and N all have proton number 89 so are the same element, and R, P and N all have $N = A - Z = 136$ neutrons.

B.explanation: M, P and S have different proton numbers 89, 90 and 91 so are not the same element.

C.explanation: M, P and S have neutron numbers 137, 136 and 135 so do not have the same number of neutrons.

D.explanation: R, P and N have different proton numbers so are not the same element, and O, P and Q have different neutron numbers.
